lines.text: Ἔχων [f. 315v] τε φράσεις καὶ λύσεις πολλῶν τρόπων
lines.en: Having [f. 315v] both expressions and solutions of many kinds
Through both disease, life, death,
Most beautiful, easily learned, all-seasonable pebbles
Of wise Petosiris and the Egyptians
Together with most lofty Pythagoras
To show victories, best one, of fighting men,
Of all matters, resourceful and resourceless
Understand, read naturally, so that you may learn
In accuracy and much safety
The clarity of all the things written;

lines.text: Καὶ οὕτω τυχὼν τοῦ ποθουμένου, φίλε,
lines.en: And thus having obtained what is desired, friend,
May we have grateful praises

lines.text: Καὶ μνήμην ἀεὶ τοῦ ἀχωρίστου βίου.
lines.en: And memory always of the inseparable life.
Here is the end with God, amen.
[D. B. and Æ. M.]
Excerpt from the Introduction of Paulus Alexandrinus.

summary.headline: Paulus Alexandrinus on Zodiac Signs
summary.text: Astrological verses invoke Astrampsychos, Petosiris, the Egyptians, and Pythagoras for divination concerning disease, life, death, and victory. An editorial note identifies a Neapolitan codex fragment as the first chapter of Paulus Alexandrinus’s Introduction to astrology, followed by its discussion of the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Aries.
